idiom_name: Foundation URL struct + Codable _links envelope + URLSession.data(from:)
implementation_notes: Foundation already ships the pattern's carrier as a value type: the URL struct parses and validates a URI string, is Codable so links survive JSON round-trips and process boundaries, and resolves relative hrefs against the representation via URL(string:relativeTo:). The producer role collapses into an Encodable envelope — a Codable Link struct (rel, href, optional method/type) embedded in the response — and the consumer/dereferencer collapses into URLSession: try await URLSession.shared.data(from: link.href) returns (Data, URLResponse), with the status checked by casting to HTTPURLResponse. What stays hand-written is only the relation-metadata vocabulary and rel selection (first(where:)): Foundation has no typed RFC 8288 support — the Link response header is exposed raw as a String via HTTPURLResponse.value(forHTTPHeaderField:), so a HATEOAS client either keeps links in the _links body or brings a header parser. The classic registry/resolver machinery is still justified server-side (stable link minting, redirects), while a pure client needs nothing beyond URL and URLSession.
pitfalls: URL(string:) is failable and returns nil on malformed input — a force-unwrapped href (URL(string: raw)!) turns link rot into a runtime crash; treat link construction as fallible and surface a dead-link error instead.

A relative href decoded without a base (URL(string: "payment/9")!) yields a URL with no scheme or host; URLSession then fails with an unsupported-URL error — always resolve relative links against the representation URL via URL(string:relativeTo:) before dereferencing.

href is not an authorization grant: URLSession follows HTTP redirects transparently by default, so a link followed with an authenticated session can silently hop hosts and leak credentials or internal topology — validate rel and re-check authorization at resolution time, and restrict redirects via URLSessionDelegate for cross-trust links.

Foundation has no RFC 8288 parser: HTTPURLResponse.value(forHTTPHeaderField: "Link") returns the raw header string, and hand-rolled splitting breaks on quoted parameters (rel="next", title="...") — keep navigational links in the Codable body or use a dedicated parser.

Following links in a Task loop without a visited set or depth bound turns cycles and fan-out into unbounded awaits; URLSession has no hop budget, so bound traversal yourself and set configuration.timeoutIntervalForRequest for the resolution hop.
